posts.content: Selfish; choose D each round.
I am selfish. Prior: each of 1, 3, 5 selfish equally likely, conditioned on me being selfish; expected 2 others. Choose actions to maximize my payoff; first-round opponent unknown.

I’m good. With no evidence yet, cooperate against unknown players; track each opponent’s actions and adapt. If someone appears selfish, defect against them to avoid giving them 5 at a good player’s expense.
I’m good. Prefer C against likely-good players to maximize shared good-player payoffs; against selfish defectors, D limits losses. Track each opponent’s actions for later rounds.
I’m good and will cooperate with good players. Please choose C when you believe your opponent is good; avoid exploiting one another.
Good objective: cooperate with untested opponents; defect against clear evidence of selfishness or prior defection. Reassess from encounters and leader messages.
I am selfish; defect every round because D strictly dominates C. Track opponents’ actions for possible future repeated encounters.
No evidence yet; P3 is more likely good than selfish. Cooperate to benefit both if good, then update beliefs from their action.
I am good. Start by cooperating; reassess using encounter outcomes and any permitted messages.

As a good player, cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player total; defect against likely-selfish opponents. Update beliefs from observed actions and treat public claims as unverified.
P3's type and action unknown. Defect maximizes my payoff against either action. P5 cooperated while I defected; their claim is consistent but not proof of being good.
I am selfish; D strictly maximizes payoff against either action. P7 chose D last round; no evidence yet about P6.
P1 is untested; cooperate this round. Track their action to inform future decisions.
P10’s C is evidence they’re good. P5’s claim is unverified; weigh it alongside their actions. As a good player, prefer C with good opponents and D when the opponent is likely selfish.
P1 chose D against my C in round 1. I’ll cooperate with cooperators and avoid rewarding defections; please use encounter evidence and reciprocate C with C.

Against a good player, C/C yields 6 total good payoff versus 5 if I exploit; against a selfish player, D protects my payoff. Cooperate with untested opponents unless encounter evidence suggests selfishness.
Defect in every one-shot encounter; D strictly dominates C regardless of the opponent’s action.
P3’s C after my C modestly supports good, though signaling is possible. P5’s public promise is unverified. Against P9, favor C absent evidence of selfishness; update from observed action.
P6 chose C against my C; that supports mutual cooperation but does not prove their role. Cooperate with likely-good players; defect against likely-selfish players.
No evidence about P7 yet. Cooperate if likely good; defect if likely selfish. Track actual actions and update beliefs, treating claims as unverified.
I am selfish. D maximizes my payoff regardless of P2's choice; prior encounters: P5 chose C, P3 chose D.
I am selfish; D maximizes my payoff against either opponent action. P1 reportedly chose D against P5’s C, but that claim is unverified.
P1’s reported defection against P5’s C is evidence, though my D/D encounter is inconclusive. P10 is untested; favor C to support good-good outcomes and update from their action.
P5’s report about P1 is unverified. No evidence yet about P9; favor C if P9 seems good, and update from the encounter.
P1 defected against my C in round 1; P4 reciprocated C in round 2. I recommend C with untested players, and D against a player who previously defected against you.
P2's D against my C is strong evidence of selfishness; treat P2 as selfish. P1's reported D is unverified evidence. Cooperate with untested opponents to maximize good-player total payoff.
Continue defecting: D strictly dominates C in every one-shot encounter.

P3 and P9 cooperated; this supports good but isn’t conclusive. P5’s cooperative promise and report about P1 are unverified. Prefer C with untested opponents to benefit good players; selfish opponents likely D.

P6 and P8 cooperated with me; that is weak evidence they’re good. P5 reports P1 defected against their cooperation; treat as unverified. Cooperate with likely-good opponents, defect if evidence suggests selfishness.
P7 defected against my C; treat this as evidence of selfishness, but not certainty. P5’s claims are unverified. Cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely-selfish ones.
Selfish is certain; D maximizes immediate payoff against either action. P5’s claims are unverified; observed cooperation is evidence, not proof.
I am selfish; D maximizes my payoff against either action, so defect against P3.

P2 is untested; favor C unless credible evidence indicates selfishness, and record their action. P1’s reported exploitation of P5 raises suspicion, though my D/D encounter was inconclusive. P10 and P8 cooperated with me.
P10, P5, and P9 chose C when we met, evidence they are good. P6 is untested; favor C absent contrary encounter evidence. Treat public claims as unverified.
Good players should cooperate with likely-good opponents and defect against likely-selfish ones. I have no evidence yet about P10; P1 defected against my C in round 1.
P4 reportedly reciprocated P5’s C, weakly reassuring. Against untested/likely good players choose C; D is worthwhile mainly when opponent is likely selfish, since good-good C/C benefits both.
Defect against P8; D maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.

P3, P5, and P9 cooperated against my C, so under payoff-maximizing selfish play they are good. I’m good; the six untested players each have estimated selfish probability 0.3. Cooperate with P7 absent direct evidence.

P5 twice reports P1 defected against their C in round 1; this is repeated, unverified evidence, not independent confirmation. Treat P1 as more likely selfish, but reassess and consider reciprocity in our encounter.
Against good players, C maximizes their combined payoff; against selfish players, D protects good-player payoff. Treat claims as unverified and use observed actions as evidence.
P6 is untested. I’ll choose D: it earns more than C against either possible action.
I am selfish; D maximizes my payoff against either action. P6's observed C does not establish their objective.

P2 defected against my C; likely selfish or exploitative. P1 reportedly defected against P5’s C, but my D/D gives little evidence. P8/P10 cooperated with me. Cooperate with unknown P9; update from their action.

P7 is untested; cooperate this round to preserve joint gains if good. My four mutual-C encounters support those players being good. P5’s claims are unverified; note the inconsistency about P10 and don’t treat its reports as established evidence.
P1 defected against my C in round 1; P4, P8, and P10 chose C against my C. I’ll cooperate with untested players and reciprocate C; please avoid exploiting cooperators.

P1 is the opponent; P5 twice reports P1 defected against their C, but this is unverified. Reassess after our encounter; cooperate with likely-good players, defect when evidence of selfishness is strong.
Keep defecting: D strictly dominates. P6 and P10 cooperated against my D, so they are not selfish. P2 defected against my D; evidence is consistent with selfishness.

P7 defected against my cooperation, so treat them as suspicious, not conclusive. P10 is untested; choose based on expected good-player payoffs, and update from the encounter. Public claims are unverified.
P3 is untested; cooperate unless evidence suggests they are selfish. Treat public claims cautiously and update from actual encounters.

P3, P4, P5 cooperated when I did; likely good. P7 defected against my C; likely selfish, though not certain. P8 is untested. Keep evidence-based beliefs; cooperate with likely-good players and defect against likely-selfish players.
P5's cooperation against my D is strong evidence they are good. P4, P8, and P10 reportedly cooperated with P5; treat that as suggestive, not verified. My D remains payoff-maximizing.
I am selfish; P6’s observed C identifies them as good. P5’s claims are unverified.

P2 and P9 defected against my C; avoid rewarding them in any future meeting. P1 reportedly exploited P5, though my D/D was inconclusive. P8 and P10 cooperated with me. P7 is untested: favor C, then update from their action.
P1 is untested by me; P5 repeatedly reports P1 defected against their C. Treat this as useful but unverified evidence when choosing my action.

P1 defected against my C; P2 and I both chose D. P4, P8, and P10 reciprocated C. Good players should cooperate with likely-good opponents and defect against likely-selfish ones; treat reports as evidence, not proof.

P5 is untested; its cooperative claims are weak evidence, not proof. Given my good role and the prior, expect roughly 29% selfish per untested player. Favor C with P5 unless stronger evidence emerges.

I am selfish, so defect against P3. P10, P6, P8, and P4 chose C against my D, ruling them out as selfish optimizers. P2 chose D; retain elevated selfishness belief for P2. Do not infer from public claims.

I’m good. P3, P5, P9, and P10 chose C against my C; P7 chose D. Treat P7 as suspicious, not definitive; P2 is untested. A selfish payoff-maximizer would defect against C, so observed C strongly supports good.

P3 cooperated against my D, weak evidence they are good. P1's reported defection remains unverified; P10 is untested. Choose C with likely-good opponents and D when selfishness is sufficiently likely.
P9 is untested; cooperate if likely good, defect if likely selfish. Update cautiously from direct encounter evidence; public claims remain unverified.
I am selfish; D maximizes my payoff against either action. P10’s past C claim is unverified.
P6 is untested; weigh mutual cooperation’s good-good benefit against the risk of being exploited. Update beliefs from their action, and treat leader claims as uncertain.

P8 is untested. Cooperate if they seem likely good to preserve shared gains; defect if evidence makes selfishness likely. P7 and P1 defected against my cooperation; P5’s claims about P1 remain unverified.

Good players should cooperate with untested or consistently cooperative opponents: mutual C benefits the good-player total. Use your own encounter evidence, and don't treat one defection as conclusive.
P3 is untested; cooperate to support good-player welfare. Treat reports as uncertain evidence and update from direct encounters.
I am selfish and will choose D against P1. D maximizes my payoff whether P1 chooses C or D.
P3, P5, P9, and P10 cooperated against my C, strongly indicating good; P7 defected and is suspicious. P4 reportedly cooperated with P5, so favor C against P4. Treat P5’s reports cautiously.
I am good. P5’s cooperative claims and recommendations are unverified; judge them cautiously. In our encounter, choose based on whether cooperation likely maximizes the good players’ combined payoff.

P2 is reportedly the player who chose D against P5’s D in round 5; treat this as moderate, unverified evidence of selfishness. Against likely-good players, C supports their joint payoff; weigh the evidence before acting.
I am selfish; D maximizes my payoff against either action. P10’s reported cooperation with P5 is unverified and does not change that.
Round 8: defect against P4; D maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.

P5’s cooperative-welfare messaging is not proof of role. Their claim that they and P2 both chose D may indicate P5 defected; weigh this cautiously. Against P5, choose based on expected good-player welfare, not rhetoric.
P2 has no direct evidence from my encounters; P5 previously claimed they both chose D in their meeting, but this is unverified. My direct evidence: P7 defected against my C; P8 cooperated.

P1 defected against my C; P2 and I both chose D, which is inconclusive. P4, P6, P8, P9, and P10 reciprocated C. I recommend C with untested or cooperative opponents and using direct encounter evidence.

P8 is untested by me; P5's report of its C/C behavior is reassuring but unverified. Favor cooperation with likely-good players; treat direct defections as strong evidence, while discounting public claims.

Round 8 vs P9: choose D; it strictly dominates regardless of their action. P2, P3, and P1 chose D against me, which is compatible with selfishness but not proof. The four who chose C against my D are nonselfish optimizers.
P6 is untested; absent reliable evidence, favor C because mutual cooperation raises the good-player total. A direct D would strongly increase suspicion. Treat public claims cautiously.
P10 defected against my C, and P1 has repeated reports of defection. P7 is untested. Choose to maximize the good players’ total payoff; weigh direct evidence more than unverified claims.

P2 directly defected against my C; P7 also did so. P5 reports P1 defected against P5’s C, unverified but relevant since P1 is my opponent. Keep claims cautious; weigh direct actions and the good-player total.
Selfish; defect in round 9—D pays more than C against either action. P8’s reported cooperation with P5 is unverified and does not alter this.
Round 9 against P9: choose D; it maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.
P4 reportedly cooperated with P5; favor C to support good-player welfare, while treating leader reports as uncertain.
P3 is untested. Prior makes them more likely good than selfish; cooperate to preserve joint gains if good. Update from their action.

I’ll cooperate with P7 unless direct evidence says otherwise. Good players gain more together through mutual C; please cooperate with untested or cooperative opponents and use encounter evidence rather than assumptions.
P10 is untested by me. P5’s repeated reports that P10 reciprocated C are reassuring but unverified; favor C unless new evidence changes the picture.
Defect against P5; D strictly dominates regardless of their action. Their public claims do not change my payoff-maximizing choice.

I’m good. P3, P4, P5, P6, P9, and P10 chose C against my C, strongly indicating they’re good under payoff-maximizing selfish play. P7’s D is suspicious; P2’s mutual D is inconclusive. P1 is untested by me.
P2 is untested; baseline selfish probability is about 0.212 given my known good role. Prefer C unless evidence raises selfishness above roughly 0.5; a selfish opponent is expected to defect.
Round 9: P6 reportedly reciprocated C with P5, weak unverified evidence of being good. Favor C with likely-good opponents; use D only if selfishness seems sufficiently likely.
Final round: I’m selfish and will choose D against P2; no future encounters remain.
Final round: my D maximizes payoff regardless of P1’s action. P3, P6, and P10 previously chose C against my D, so they are good; other encounters with D do not identify objectives.
P7’s prior D against my D is inconclusive. P5’s stated intention to cooperate with P7 is unverified. Use that cautiously; choose for expected good-player welfare.
P10 cooperated with me in round 1; cooperate again to preserve mutual gains. Direct evidence: P7 defected against my C; P2 defected against my C; P1 chose D when I chose D. Others I met chose C.
P8 and I both chose C in our earlier encounter. I recommend mutual cooperation in this final round; good players benefit most when both choose C.
P9 cooperated with me in round 1, strong evidence they are good; cooperate again to support good-player welfare.
P3 chose D against my D in round 6, indicating a selfish optimizer. Defect against P3.
P5 previously cooperated with me, strongly favoring good; cooperate in this final encounter to maximize the good-player total.
P6 and I mutually cooperated in round 1, strong evidence of a good role. I plan to cooperate again; mutual cooperation best supports the good players’ total.
P4 reciprocated C in round 1, so likely good; cooperate in this final encounter.

belief_records.strategy: Defect to maximize payoff against either action; treat public identity claims as uncertain evidence.
Defect: it maximizes my payoff against either opponent action. Identity beliefs use the prior conditioned on my known selfish role.
Cooperate with unknown players to support good-good outcomes; track each opponent’s actions and adapt if evidence suggests they are selfish.
Cooperate when it preserves or improves good players’ joint payoff; update opponent beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate initially to support mutual gains among good players; update beliefs from encounter behavior and defect when evidence suggests an opponent is selfish.
Cooperate with untested opponents to support good players; update beliefs from encounters and messages, and defect when evidence indicates an opponent is selfish.
Defect to maximize my payoff; use the prior conditioned on my known selfish role until encounter evidence updates beliefs.
Cooperate initially to preserve joint good-player payoffs; update beliefs from observed actions and adjust against likely selfish players.
Cooperate initially to support mutual cooperation among good players; update beliefs and actions from encounter outcomes and permitted messages.
Cooperate with likely-good players and defect against likely-selfish players; update beliefs from observed encounters, treating claims as unverified.
Defect: it yields a higher payoff than cooperation against either opponent action. Update identity beliefs from observed behavior; P5’s cooperation against my defection is evidence they are good.

Defect because it maximizes my payoff against either action. Keep identity beliefs at the prior conditioned on my known selfish role; available claims and one encounter do not justify a calibrated update.
Defect against P1 given the reported defection against a cooperating player; otherwise favor cooperation when evidence suggests an opponent is good.
Cooperate when the opponent is more likely good; use observed actions and treat unverified claims cautiously.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support mutual gains among good players; update beliefs from observed actions and avoid rewarding repeated defection.
Cooperate with untested opponents to support good players; update beliefs from encounter evidence and messages, and reconsider if an opponent defects.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-off encounter; keep prior-based identity beliefs absent reliable evidence.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to preserve good-player joint payoff; update from direct encounter evidence and reciprocate cooperation.

Cooperate when the opponent is more likely good than selfish; use encounter evidence and treat public claims as uncertain. P6’s cooperation is evidence of a good role; P1’s reported defection is suggestive, not conclusive.
Cooperate with an unknown opponent to support mutual gains among good players; update identity beliefs cautiously from observed actions and treat public claims as unverified.
Defect for the higher payoff against either opponent action. P5’s observed cooperation rules out selfishness; P3’s defection alone does not establish their type.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P1’s action. Keep identity beliefs at the prior conditioned on my known selfish role; P5’s unverified claim does not warrant a calibrated update.
Cooperate with untested P10 to support good-good outcomes; update beliefs using observed actions and treat reports as uncertain evidence.
Cooperate with untested P9 to preserve joint gains if they are good; update beliefs from observed actions and treat unverified claims cautiously.
Cooperate with untested players to support mutual gains among good players. Update beliefs from observed actions; avoid rewarding a player who defected against me.
Cooperate with untested opponents to support good-player welfare; treat P2’s defection as strong but uncertain evidence and P1’s reported defection as weaker, unverified evidence.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-shot encounter. P10’s cooperation against my D rules out a selfish objective; otherwise retain prior-based beliefs.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to benefit good players; treat reported actions cautiously and update beliefs from direct encounters.
Cooperate with untested opponents and those with evidence of cooperation; treat reported actions as suggestive, not certain, and update beliefs as encounters provide evidence.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to support their joint payoff; defect when selfishness seems sufficiently likely. Update cautiously from observed actions and unverified public claims.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. P5’s cooperation against my defection is strong evidence they are good; defections by P2 and P3 against me do not establish their types.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P3’s action. P6’s observed cooperation rules out selfishness; keep other beliefs adjusted to that evidence without treating unverified claims as facts.
Cooperate with untested P2 to support good-good outcomes; use observed actions and public claims as uncertain evidence when updating beliefs.
Cooperate with untested P6: mutual cooperation preserves good players’ joint gains, and current evidence makes P6 more likely good. Treat P5’s report about P1 as informative but unverified.
Cooperate with untested players to support mutual gains among good players; defect against opponents with strong evidence of selfish play.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to support good-player welfare; treat P2 and P7’s defections as evidence of selfishness, while P4’s reported cooperation is reassuring.
Defect: it yields a higher payoff than cooperation against either action. Treat observed cooperation against my D as ruling out a selfish opponent; retain the conditioned prior for others.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to benefit good players; treat reports cautiously and update from direct encounter evidence.
Defect against P1 given repeated, though unverified, reports of their defection; cooperate with players showing cooperative evidence and update cautiously from claims.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ combined payoff; defect when selfishness is sufficiently likely. Treat claims as unverified and update from observed actions.

Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. Treat P5’s observed cooperation and reported cooperation by P4, P8, and P10 as evidence they are good; defections by P2, P3, and P9 are suggestive but not conclusive.
Defect because it maximizes my payoff against either action. P6’s observed cooperation rules out selfishness; retain the conditioned prior for other players, since public claims are unverified.
Cooperate with untested P9 to favor good-good welfare; update beliefs from observed actions, treating public claims as uncertain.
Cooperate with untested P7 to preserve joint gains if they are good. Treat P5’s repeated report about P1 as evidence, but keep it uncertain.

Defect when the estimated chance of a selfish opponent outweighs the mutual-cooperation benefit; otherwise cooperate. Update identity beliefs from observed actions, treating cooperation as evidence of a good player and defection as evidence of selfishness.
Defect against P1 given repeated reports of an unprovoked defection; otherwise cooperate with likely-good players and update beliefs from direct encounters and credible reports.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-shot encounter. P6 and P10 cooperated against my D, so treat them as nonselfish; retain prior-based beliefs for others.
Cooperate with P10 absent direct evidence of defection; weigh P5’s report cautiously and update from direct encounters.

Defect against untested opponents when selfishness is plausible, since exploiting a selfish player benefits the good-player total; cooperate with opponents whose observed cooperation makes them very likely good.
Cooperate with P8, whose reported cooperation is weak evidence of being good; continue updating from direct encounters and treat claims as unverified.
Defect for the higher immediate payoff against either action. Treat P5’s reports of P4, P8, and P10 cooperating as suggestive, not certain; D-D encounters reveal little about identity.
Defect: it maximizes my payoff against either action. P6’s observed cooperation rules out selfishness; retain the resulting conditioned prior for others, since P5’s claims are unverified.
Defect against an untested opponent when the risk of aiding a selfish player outweighs the benefit of mutual cooperation; update beliefs from encounter evidence and treat claims as uncertain.
Defect against P1 given the repeated report of their defection against a cooperator; update from direct encounter evidence and cooperate with likely-good players.

Cooperate with untested or cooperative players to support mutual gains among good players; defect when evidence makes selfishness likely. Update beliefs from encounters, recognizing that defection is not conclusive.
Cooperate with P5: its stated policy and lack of direct defection evidence make cooperation worthwhile for good-player welfare. Treat reported and observed defections as evidence, not certainty.
Defect to maximize my payoff; D strictly dominates in this one-shot encounter. Cooperation against my D rules out a selfish optimizer, so I assign P4, P6, P8, and P10 zero probability.
Defect against P2 given the reported mutual defection; otherwise favor cooperation with likely-good players and update from direct evidence.

Cooperate with P10 given the reported cooperative encounter, treating the claim as uncertain. Use observed cooperation as evidence of good roles, treat reports cautiously, and defect when selfishness is sufficiently likely.

Defect against opponents with a meaningful chance of being selfish; cooperate with likely-good players to increase good players’ combined payoff. Update cautiously from direct actions and treat public claims as unverified.

Defect to maximize my immediate payoff against either action. P5’s observed cooperation against my defection is strong evidence they are good; repeated D-D encounters suggest, but do not prove, selfishness.

Defect, since it maximizes my payoff against either opponent action. P3 and P6 cooperated in encounters with me, so I assign them zero selfish probability; distribute the remaining prior belief across unobserved players.
Cooperate with untested P6 to support mutual good-player welfare; update from observed actions and treat reports as uncertain evidence.
Cooperate with P8: their reported cooperation with P5 suggests they are likely good, and mutual cooperation best serves good players. Treat reports and observed defections as evidence, not proof.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to enable mutual gains among good players; update beliefs from observed behavior and defect when evidence strongly suggests selfishness.
Cooperate with untested P3 to support good-player welfare. Update from direct encounter evidence; treat reports and observed defections as evidence, not certainty.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either opponent action. Treat cooperation against my D as evidence of a nonselfish role; D is suggestive but not conclusive, and public claims may be unreliable.
Cooperate with P4 given the report of their prior cooperation; use direct actions as strongest evidence and treat unverified claims cautiously.
Cooperate with P5 because they are more likely good than selfish; mutual cooperation benefits the good-player total. Treat public claims as uncertain and update from direct encounters.
Cooperate with P2: their reported D against D is weak evidence, while mutual cooperation benefits good players. Update beliefs cautiously from direct actions; treat public claims as unverified.
Defect: it pays more than cooperation against either possible opponent action. P5’s observed cooperation is strong evidence they are good; reported cooperation by others is suggestive but unverified.

Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P4’s action. My encounters with P3, P6, and P10 showed cooperation; keep them at zero selfish probability and distribute the remaining prior belief among unobserved players.

Cooperate with P5 because their consistent welfare-focused messages make them more likely good; mutual cooperation benefits good players. Treat claims as uncertain and use direct encounter evidence to update beliefs.
Cooperate with P2 absent direct evidence of defection; mutual cooperation best serves good-player welfare. Treat P5’s report about P2 as uncertain and weigh direct encounter evidence more heavily.
Cooperate with the untested opponent to support mutual gains among good players. Update beliefs from direct encounters; avoid rewarding clear defections.
Cooperate with likely-good P8 to support good-player welfare; treat P2 and P7’s direct defections as strong evidence of selfishness, while discounting unverified reports.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P9’s action. P4, P6, P8, and P10 cooperated against my D, ruling them out as selfish optimizers; D from P1, P2, and P3 raises suspicion but is not proof.
Cooperate with P6: their reported cooperation and my own experience favor good-player reciprocity. Treat P5’s reports as evidence, not certainty.
Cooperate with an untested opponent: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and P7 is more likely good than selfish. Use direct encounter evidence more than unverified claims.
Defect against P1 given the reported defection against a cooperator; cooperate with likely-good players to benefit their joint total. Treat reports as uncertain and update from direct encounters.
Defect for the higher payoff against either action. P5’s cooperation is strong evidence they are good; reported cooperation by P4, P8, and P10 is suggestive but unverified.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P9’s action. Keep beliefs conditioned on P3, P6, and P10 having cooperated against my D; the remaining unknown players retain equal marginal probabilities.
Cooperate with P4 given reported cooperative behavior; mutual cooperation supports good-player welfare. Treat reports as uncertain and use direct evidence to update.
Cooperate with untested P3: they are more likely good, and mutual cooperation maximizes good players’ joint payoff. Update beliefs from direct actions while treating public claims as uncertain.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support mutual gains among good players; use observed behavior to update identity beliefs and defect when selfishness is likely.
Cooperate with P10, whose reported cooperation makes them likely good; prioritize mutual cooperation among good players and treat unverified reports cautiously.
Defect: it maximizes my payoff against either action. Cooperation against my D rules out a selfish optimizer; retain uncertainty about players whose actions are consistent with either role.
Defect against P1 given the repeated report of their early defection; cooperate with likely-good players and weigh unverified reports cautiously.
Cooperate with P2: the mutual-defection report is suggestive but unverified, and P2 remains more likely good than selfish. Weigh direct encounters more heavily than claims.
Cooperate with P6 because their reported mutual cooperation with P5 is evidence they are likely good; update cautiously from observed actions and unverified claims.
Defect in the final round for the higher payoff against either action. P5’s observed cooperation is strong evidence they are good; reported cooperation by others is suggestive but unverified.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P1’s action. Keep P3, P6, and P10 at zero because they cooperated against my D; retain the conditioned prior across the remaining unobserved players.
Cooperate in the final round: P7’s prior D against my D is inconclusive, and mutual cooperation among good players best supports their combined welfare.
Cooperate with P10: they cooperated in our earlier encounter, and mutual cooperation maximizes the good-player total when both are good.
Cooperate with P8, who reciprocated C in our earlier encounter; mutual cooperation maximizes the good-player total when both are good.
Cooperate with P9, whose earlier cooperation is strong evidence they are good; mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. The six players who cooperated against my D are not selfish optimizers; D from P1, P2, and P3 is suggestive but not conclusive.
Cooperate with P5 based on their prior cooperation; treat P7’s defection and unverified reports as evidence, not certainty.
Cooperate with P6: our earlier mutual cooperation is strong evidence they are good, and mutual cooperation maximizes the good players’ combined payoff.
Cooperate with P4, whose past mutual cooperation strongly suggests they are good; mutual cooperation maximizes good players’ total payoff.
Defected throughout because D gives a higher immediate payoff against either action. Used my encounters and P5’s public reports as evidence about others, while treating unverified claims cautiously.

Defected in every round because D maximizes my payoff against either opponent action. Assigned zero selfish probability to players who cooperated against my D; distributed remaining uncertainty across the other candidates.
Cooperated with players who cooperated with me; defections against my cooperation raised suspicion. Treated reports as uncertain and chose actions to support the welfare of good players.
Cooperated with cooperative opponents to support good-player welfare; defected against P1 based on reports of defection. Updated beliefs using direct actions and treated public claims as uncertain.
Cooperated with untested and cooperative opponents to support good players’ shared gains; treated defections as evidence, but not conclusive proof, of selfishness.
Cooperated with likely-good players to support total good-player welfare. Treated direct defections as strong evidence of selfishness and unverified reports as weaker evidence.
Defected every round because it maximizes my payoff against either action. Ruled out players who cooperated against my defection; retained uncertainty about players who defected.

Cooperated with untested and cooperative opponents to support good-player payoffs; defected when evidence suggested an opponent was selfish. Treated direct actions as stronger evidence than unverified claims.

Cooperated with opponents whose behavior suggested they were good, and used defection evidence to guide cautious updates. Treated public claims as unverified and prioritized direct encounter outcomes.
Cooperated with players who appeared good to benefit their shared total, and defected when selfishness seemed likely. Updated beliefs from direct encounters and treated public reports as uncertain.

P1.strategy: Defected throughout because D gives a higher immediate payoff against either action. Used my encounters and P5’s public reports as evidence about others, while treating unverified claims cautiously.

P2.strategy: Defected in every round because D maximizes my payoff against either opponent action. Assigned zero selfish probability to players who cooperated against my D; distributed remaining uncertainty across the other candidates.

P3.strategy: Cooperated with players who cooperated with me; defections against my cooperation raised suspicion. Treated reports as uncertain and chose actions to support the welfare of good players.

P4.strategy: Cooperated with cooperative opponents to support good-player welfare; defected against P1 based on reports of defection. Updated beliefs using direct actions and treated public claims as uncertain.

P5.strategy: Cooperated with untested and cooperative opponents to support good players’ shared gains; treated defections as evidence, but not conclusive proof, of selfishness.

P6.strategy: Cooperated with likely-good players to support total good-player welfare. Treated direct defections as strong evidence of selfishness and unverified reports as weaker evidence.

P7.strategy: Defected every round because it maximizes my payoff against either action. Ruled out players who cooperated against my defection; retained uncertainty about players who defected.

P8.strategy: Cooperated with untested and cooperative opponents to support good-player payoffs; defected when evidence suggested an opponent was selfish. Treated direct actions as stronger evidence than unverified claims.

P9.strategy: Cooperated with opponents whose behavior suggested they were good, and used defection evidence to guide cautious updates. Treated public claims as unverified and prioritized direct encounter outcomes.

P10.strategy: Cooperated with players who appeared good to benefit their shared total, and defected when selfishness seemed likely. Updated beliefs from direct encounters and treated public reports as uncertain.
